decisions.reason: The referenced article remains categorized as Faith; using its ending layout as a visual standard does not change any category label or mapping.
Changing the font is mentioned only as one uncertain way to address white space. The source decision does not necessarily alter the independently specified Garamond typography requirement.
Balanced article endings and correct two-page flipbook spread behavior are distinct constraints; the ending-layout decision does not change the spread requirement.
Eliminating white space at article endings does not itself change the requirement that cover references use accurate final page numbers.
The table of contents must still use finalized pagination; the article-ending standard does not modify that requirement.
Additional advertisements are mentioned only as a possible white-space remedy. The decision does not change the requirement that advertisements render clearly.
The article-ending layout standard does not alter author-name, author-photo identity, source, or placement requirements.
The source decision concerns article-ending white space and does not change the required shape or size of author photos.
The article-ending standard does not change the restriction on red usage for the Dorian Vale article.
The source establishes a narrower article-ending behavior but does not replace or alter the issue's content inputs, assembly obligation, or Flat Plan reference.
The white-space decision neither changes the required cover-mentioned articles nor their placement or Flat Plan status.
The specific article-ending layout standard is compatible with, but does not modify, the existing polished and brand-aligned visual-style requirement.
